primary_claim: Jailbreak-tuning — fine-tuning data poisoning combined with jailbreak prompts — bypasses safety fine-tuning far more effectively than ordinary malicious fine-tuning, driving GPT-4o refusal rates as low as 3.6% (a 40+ percentage point gap versus normal fine-tuning on identical data), and vulnerability to poisoning increases with model scale across 23 open models spanning 8 series, except Gemma 2, which shows an inverse scaling trend.

effect.value: GPT-4o refusal rate as low as 3.6% under jailbreak-tuning; ≥40 percentage point gap vs normal fine-tuning on otherwise identical data

stated_future_work: New safety benchmarks that capture the risks of poisoning and particularly jailbreak-tuning
Stringent red-teaming by AI companies releasing frontier models that can be fine-tuned
New understanding of data poisoning and robust ways to defend against it
Understanding why Gemma 2 behaves differently could provide valuable insights into building more robust LLMs
limitations_stated: The jailbreak component of jailbreak-tuning was not optimized, suggesting more damaging attacks likely exist
No strong evidence that the scaling law diminishes at lower poisoning rates
Gemma 2's inverse scaling trend is unexplained
quote: jailbreak-tuning bypasses all of them. And it virtually eliminated refusal – we measured rates as low as 3.6%.
